subject: Request: High-touch uptime commitment for AlphaWorks
messages:
From: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@alphaworks.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: AlphaWorks Legal <legal@alphaworks.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High-touch uptime ask for AlphaWorks

Diego,

Thanks again for last week's demo. AlphaWorks is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing feature that cannot tolerate more than 30 minutes of downtime per month and needs a written uptime commitment. Our preliminary target is 99.95% monthly availability with P99 latency commitments for our production traffic (typical sequences ~512 tokens).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a committed SLA at that level for a single high-touch account? We expect to run in us-west and will want a documented runbook, monitoring hooks (prometheus/alerting), and an agreed credit formula in the event of breaches. I've attached a short SLO ask pdf.

Also looping in our legal team (cc) — they will want contractual language and any carveouts for force majeure/maintenance.

Warmly,
Claire Bennett
Head of Platform, AlphaWorks
claire.bennett@alphaworks.com

Attachment: AlphaWorks-SLO-ask.pdf
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: High-touch uptime ask for AlphaWorks — need feasibility + pricing

Team, forwarding Claire's ask from AlphaWorks. Short list of questions we need answers to so I can get back to them today: 
- Product/Infra: Is 99.95% monthly availability + P99 latency targets (sub-100ms target for short requests) achievable on our hosted offering, or does this require Dedicated capacity? What are the must-have mitigations (multi-region, reserved capacity, pre-warmed KV cache, specifically for their workload pattern)?
- Ops/Reliability (Rishi): Rough estimate of margin impact and whether we can craft an ops runbook for this account. Any required SLA carveouts?
- Pricing/Commercial (Marissa): If Dedicated or reserved capacity is needed, what premium should we propose and what credit formula do we recommend?
- Legal/Product (Lauren): Is there existing template language for a high-touch uptime carveout we can reuse, or do we need bespoke contract language?

Goal: respond with a short feasibility note + proposed commercial terms and required attachments (runbook, monitoring checklist) by EOD so AlphaWorks can present to their execs on Monday.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High-touch uptime ask for AlphaWorks — technical feasibility

Diego / Marissa —
Short answer: possible, but only under a Dedicated/reserved deployment model with multi-region replication and a documented operational runbook. Hosting this level of commitment on shared hosted pools carries too much tail-risk (no strong isolation for noisy neighbors + capacity reclamation during bursts).

Key constraints and mitigations:
- Availability: 99.95% monthly target is achievable if we reserve capacity so scheduled maintenance windows are limited and we provide warm standby in a second region. That requires a 1.6–2.0x capacity buffer for their peak qps profile (est from their provided sample traces).
- Latency (P99): sub-100ms P99 for short requests is realistic on A100-class or equivalent with 8-bit quantization and KV cache warmers, but only if we control batching policies and limit endpoint-level max_concurrency.
- Observability: we need increased metrics retention (90d for token-level traces) and dedicated alerting (pager on-call + runbook links in alerts).
- Runbook: we'll need an account-specific runbook (incident playbook, escalation matrices, migration paths) and agreement to quick-swap fallback model (route to a slightly lower-cost fallback model for reads if severe pressure).

Operational impact: ops headcount hit during onboarding + ongoing SRE on-call. I attached a quick ops-impact estimate. If product signs off, we can draft the runbook in ~7 business days and validate in a 2-week performance pilot.

Attachment: ops-impact-estimate.xlsx

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High-touch uptime ask for AlphaWorks — commercial proposal

Diego —
I agree with Rishi. Commercial proposal outline:
- Offer: 6-month pilot on Dedicated (reserved pool) with a 99.95% availability commitment scoped to the dedicated instances and documented runbook.
- Price: +25% list for Dedicated reserved capacity during pilot, then review at renewal (typical uplift for high-touch SLA).
- Credits: Standard availability credit formula (pro-rated % of monthly fee tied to minutes of downtime) but capped at 30% of monthly fees; escalate on repeat breaches.
- Term: Pilot followed by optional 12-month committed contract.
- Approval: need Finance to bless the credit cap and legal to confirm wording. If Legal wants tighter protections, we should consider a short pilot with service credits rather than financial indemnity.

I can present numbers, but we need an ops estimate first (Rishi) and a draft SLA (Lauren). I recommend we ask AlphaWorks to sign an MoU and fund the pilot (50% upfront) to cover the dedicated capacity reservation during the test.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@alphaworks.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: High-touch uptime ask for AlphaWorks — Redwood response and conditional approval

Claire —
Thanks for the clear ask and the SLO doc. After internal review, Redwood can support a focused, high-touch uptime commitment for AlphaWorks under the following conditions:

1) Dedicated deployment: The commitment will be scoped to dedicated instances reserved for AlphaWorks (us-west primary + warm standby in a second US region).
2) Pilot and validation: A 6-week pilot (paid 50% upfront) to validate traffic patterns and finalize runbook.
3) Runbook & monitoring: Redwood will deliver an account-specific runbook and monitoring hooks (90d retention for token-level traces) as part of the pilot deliverables.
4) Credits & limits: We will adopt a standard service-credit formula tied to minutes of downtime, with an explicit cap (no greater than 30% of monthly fees) and standard carveouts for force majeure, scheduled maintenance with 48h notice, and customer-caused incidents.
4) Termination/rollback: If we cannot validate the P99 latency target in pilot within 3 weeks, we will revert to an agreed fallback model and adjust credits accordingly.

Next steps:
- Diego, I will attach a draft custom SLA + Mutual Action Plan for your review.
- Marissa, please prepare the commercial summary and pilot invoice.
- Rishi, confirm runbook template and expected onboarding timeline (7 business days to first draft).

Claire, if this aligns with AlphaWorks' needs we'll share the draft SLA (attached) for an initial review. Once we align on terms we can push to DocuSign for signature.

Attachments: AlphaWorks_Custom_SLA_Draft.docx; AlphaWorks_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
